not_modelled.what: DC and federal government survivor benefits (D-40 Line 12) are subtracted in full for an annuitant's survivor aged 62 or older at the end of the year (not Social Security survivor benefits). A projection does not know that a pension is a survivor annuity from the DC or federal government.
Additional standard deduction of 1,600 (2,000 if single or head of household) for each filer or spouse who is blind.

Up to 10,000 of income excluded for a person the Social Security Administration found totally and permanently disabled and receiving disability benefits, when annual household adjusted gross income is under 100,000 (Schedule I Calculation B Line 7a).
Interest and dividends on US Treasury and other US government obligations are subtracted (Schedule I Calculation B Line 1).

approximations.what: Government and private pensions, IRA and employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions are taxed as part of federal AGI, as the booklet prints no relief for them; DC and federal government survivor benefits for a survivor aged 62 or older (Line 12) are taxed too because survivor status is not known.
approximations.size: Only for a survivor annuitant 62 or older: up to 8.5% of the survivor benefit (a 30,000 survivor annuity at 8.5%: 2,550 a year); none for other households.

approximations.what: The DC standard deduction is always taken. DC requires the same deduction type as the federal return; DC itemized deductions (no state and local income taxes, real estate taxes in full, reduced by 5% of DC AGI over 200,000) are not modelled.
approximations.size: For a federal itemizer, the bracket rate times the difference between the DC itemized deductions and the DC standard deduction.

approximations.what: Railroad retirement is exempted in full; the booklet's Line 10 names only tier 1, so tier 2 railroad retirement (taxed in DC) is exempted as well.
approximations.size: The bracket rate times tier 2 benefits included in federal AGI.

approximations.what: The additional standard deduction for blindness and the disability exclusion are not applied.
approximations.size: Up to 2,000 x 8.5% = 170 per blind person; up to 10,000 x the bracket rate for the disability exclusion.

approximations.what: Interest on US Treasury obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
approximations.size: The bracket rate times the Treasury interest and dividends.

approximations.what: A projection that cannot tell DC bonds from other states' bonds treats all tax-exempt interest as other-state and adds it back.
approximations.size: The bracket rate times interest from DC, territory, DC Water, WMATA and DCHFA obligations.

approximations.what: Married couples are projected as married_joint or married_separate; filing separately on the same return (30,000 standard deduction, each spouse taxed on the schedule separately) is not modelled, and a separate filer's spouse age-65 amount (allowed only if the spouse has no gross income) is not checked.
approximations.size: Small for most couples; separate filing on the same return can lower tax when incomes are very unequal.

approximations.what: Tax on taxable income of 100,000 or less comes from the tax tables (50-dollar rows); the projection uses the rate schedule.
Additions to federal AGI other than out-of-state bond interest (qualified small business stock gain excluded under IRC 1202, business items) are not modelled.
approximations.size: The bracket rate times the excluded gain, for a household that sells qualified small business stock.
